name: Burden of Longitude
description:
Burden of Longitude formed in 2206 through what remains one of the stranger origin stories in GLMZ music: a Tier 2 welder named Cass Oduya-Brennan posted a raw acoustic recording to a pirate mesh node, and it was heard the same week by both a Tier 1 poet named Xiulan Ferreira-Nkosi and a Tier 4 session musician named Jørgen Abebe-Yamamoto, who had been quietly burning out inside the Vantablack studio system for years. All three showed up to the same illegal venue on a rumor, played together for the first time, and by the end of the night had become something none of them could individually explain. The band's sound sits in a space that has no comfortable genre home: Oduya-Brennan's raw guitar work draws from Delta blues and Saharan desert rock, Ferreira-Nkosi's spoken-word vocals weave Mandarin, Yoruba, and English in structures closer to poetry than lyric, and Abebe-Yamamoto's production instincts bring a Spire-trained precision that somehow never bleeds the rawness out.

They have no legal releases. Every recording in circulation was captured at one of their illegal shows — which are announced six hours in advance through encrypted mesh networks and draw audiences from every tier, people who have no other reason to be in the same room together. Corporate security has raided seven of their shows. They have never been caught.
creator: Cass Oduya-Brennan
genre: cross-tier fusion, spoken word blues, desert rock, mesh folk
audience: Cross-tier audiences drawn by word of mouth — Tier 1 activists, Tier 2 workers, Tier 3 dissatisfied professionals, Tier 4 dropouts, occasional Spire observers
cultural_impact: Burden of Longitude has become an unlikely symbol of the possibility — however fragile ��� of cross-tier solidarity in GLMZ. Their shows are one of the few spaces where the social architecture of the city briefly dissolves, where a Shelf resident and a Tier 4 corporate analyst stand in the same dark room listening to the same thing. Vantablack Media has attempted to sign them through intermediaries twice and been refused both times. Cultural commentators have written more words about what Burden of Longitude means than the band has ever said publicly. The members give no interviews. The music speaks, and people keep finding it.
story_hooks: A Vantablack Media fixer has been tasked not with shutting the band down but with identifying and quietly neutralizing the encrypted mesh network they use to announce shows — someone has hired the players to protect that network.

Jørgen Abebe-Yamamoto's Tier 4 background has surfaced in a Shelf publication as a suspected corporate plant, and the accusation — false or not — is tearing apart the fragile cross-tier community the band has built.

A recording from an early Burden of Longitude show contains background audio that places a specific Spire executive at a Tier 1 location on a night when a significant 'industrial accident' occurred — someone wants the recording, and someone else wants it destroyed.
